categories.name: General
categories.description: TLP service, profile switching and diagnostic behavior.

settings.description: Enable/disable TLP

Set to 1 to deactivate all intrinsic defaults of TLP. This means that
TLP only applies settings that have been explicitly activated i.e.
parameters without a leading '#'.
Notes:
- Helpful if one wants to use only selected features of TLP
- After activation, use tlp-stat -c to display your effective configuration

Control how warnings about invalid settings are issued:
0=disabled,
1=background tasks (boot, resume, change of power source) report to syslog,
2=shell commands report to the terminal (stderr),
3=combination of 1 and 2

Colorize error, warning, notice and success messages.
Colors are specified with ANSI codes:
1=bold black, 90=grey, 91=red, 92=green, 93=yellow, 94=blue, 95=magenta, 96=cyan, 97=white.
Other colors are possible, refer to:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#3-bit_and_4-bit
Colors must be specified in the order "error, warning, notice, success".
By default, errors are shown in red, warnings in yellow, notices in bold and success in green

Control automatic switching of the power profile when connecting or removing
the charger, when booting the system or when executing 'tlp start':
0=disabled - never switch, use TLP_DEFAULT_MODE if configured
1=auto - always switch, select performance on AC and
balanced on battery power.
2=smart - do not switch if the following profiles were active previously:
power-saver or balanced on AC resp.
power-saver or performance on battery power.
Note: the same applies if the charger was connected/removed during suspend

Power supply classes to ignore when determining operation mode: AC, USB, BAT.
Separate multiple classes with spaces.
Note: try on laptops where operation mode AC/BAT is incorrectly detected

groups.title: TLP ENABLE
groups.description: Turn TLP power management on or off.

groups.title: TLP DISABLE DEFAULTS
groups.description: Use only settings explicitly enabled below. Leave this off unless you want a fully manual TLP configuration.

groups.title: TLP WARN LEVEL
groups.description: Choose where TLP reports configuration warnings.

groups.title: TLP MSG COLORS
groups.description: ANSI color codes for error, warning, notice, and success messages, in that order.

groups.title: TLP AUTO SWITCH
groups.description: Select how TLP switches profiles when the power source changes.

groups.title: TLP PROFILE
groups.description: Map AC, battery, and fallback states to TLP profiles. AC/BAT remain available as legacy aliases.

groups.title: TLP PS IGNORE
groups.description: Ignore selected power-supply classes when TLP detects AC or battery mode. Use only if detection is wrong.

categories.name: Audio
categories.description: Audio controller power saving on AC and battery.

settings.description:
Disable controller too (HDA only): Y/N.
Note: effective only when SOUND_POWER_SAVE_ON_AC/BAT is activated

groups.title: SOUND POWER SAVE
groups.description: Intel HDA/AC97 audio · Set the idle timeout before power saving; 0 disables it.

groups.title: SOUND POWER SAVE CONTROLLER
groups.description: HDA only · Power down the controller when audio power saving is active.

categories.name: Disks
categories.description: Disk idle, APM, I/O scheduler, SATA and AHCI runtime power.

settings.description:
Define disk devices on which the following DISK/AHCI_RUNTIME parameters act.
Separate multiple devices with spaces.
Devices can be specified by disk ID also (lookup with: tlp diskid)

Exclude disk classes from advanced power management (APM):
- sata, ata, usb, ieee1394.
Separate multiple classes with spaces.
CAUTION: USB and IEEE1394 disks may fail to mount or data may get corrupted with APM enabled.
Be careful and make sure you have backups of all affected media before removing 'usb' or 'ieee1394' from the denylist(!)

Select io scheduler for the disk devices: noop/deadline/cfq (Default: cfq)
Separate values for multiple devices with spaces

Exclude SATA links from AHCI link power management (ALPM).
SATA links are specified by their host. Refer to the output of
tlp-stat -d to determine the host; the format is "hostX".
Separate multiple hosts with spaces
Seconds of inactivity before disk is suspended
Optical drive device to power off (default sr0)

groups.title: DISK IDLE SECS
groups.description: Delay before syncing an idle disk; 0 disables laptop mode.

groups.title: MAX LOST WORK SECS
groups.description: Maximum age of dirty pages before they are written to disk.

groups.title: DISK DEVICES
groups.description: Target disks for disk and AHCI settings. Separate device names or tlp diskid IDs with spaces.

groups.title: DISK APM LEVEL
groups.description: Hard-disk APM level per device. Lower values save more power; 255 disables APM. Levels 1–127 may spin disks down.

groups.title: DISK APM CLASS DENYLIST
groups.description: Disk classes excluded from APM. Keep USB and IEEE 1394 excluded unless you understand the data-loss risk.

groups.title: DISK SPINDOWN TIMEOUT
groups.description: Hard-disk spin-down timeout in hdparm units; 0 disables spin-down.

groups.title: DISK IOSCHED
groups.description: I/O scheduler per target disk. Separate multiple values with spaces.

groups.title: SATA LINKPWR
groups.description: SATA/AHCI link power policy. Aggressive modes save more power but may reduce compatibility.

groups.title: SATA LINKPWR DENYLIST
groups.description: SATA hosts excluded from link power management. Find host names with tlp-stat -d.

groups.title: AHCI RUNTIME PM
groups.description: Runtime power management for NVMe, SATA, ATA, USB disks, and SATA ports.

groups.title: AHCI RUNTIME PM TIMEOUT
groups.description: Idle time before managed disks enter runtime suspend.

groups.title: BAY POWEROFF
groups.description: Power off supported optical drives in UltraBay/MediaBay. Hard disks are never powered off.

groups.title: BAY DEVICE
groups.description: Optical-drive device to power off, usually sr0.

categories.name: Graphics
categories.description: Intel and AMD graphics power and frequency policy.

groups.title: INTEL GPU POWER PROFILE
groups.description: Intel Xe only · Select the xe-driver power profile.

groups.title: INTEL GPU FREQ
groups.description: Intel only · Set supported GPU min, max, and boost frequencies. Check tlp-stat -g.

groups.title: RADEON DPM PERF LEVEL
groups.description: AMD only · Select the DPM level for amdgpu/radeon; Automatic is recommended.

groups.title: AMDGPU ABM LEVEL
groups.description: AMD Vega+ only · Set panel ABM strength. Higher levels save more power but may affect color.

settings.description: Disable wake on LAN

groups.title: WIFI PWR
groups.description: Wi-Fi power-saving policy for AC and battery profiles.

groups.title: WOL DISABLE
groups.description: Disable Wake-on-LAN to reduce idle network power.

categories.name: PCIe
categories.description: PCIe ASPM and runtime power management.

settings.description:
Exclude listed PCIe device adresses from Runtime PM.
Note: this preserves the kernel driver default, to force a certain state
- use RUNTIME_PM_ENABLE/DISABLE instead.
Separate multiple addresses with spaces.
Use lspci to get the addresses (1st column)

Exclude PCIe devices assigned to the listed drivers from Runtime PM.
Note: this preserves the kernel driver default, to force a certain state
- use RUNTIME_PM_ENABLE/DISABLE instead.
Separate multiple drivers with spaces.
Leave empty to disable completely

groups.title: PCIE ASPM
groups.description: PCIe link power policy. System default is the safest choice.

groups.title: RUNTIME PM
groups.description: Runtime power management for PCIe devices.

groups.title: RUNTIME PM DENYLIST
groups.description: PCIe addresses excluded from Runtime PM. Find addresses with lspci.

groups.title: RUNTIME PM DRIVER DENYLIST
groups.description: Exclude all PCIe devices using listed drivers. Separate driver names with spaces.

groups.title: RUNTIME PM DEVICE
groups.description: Force Runtime PM on or off for listed PCIe addresses. These rules take priority.

categories.name: Processor
categories.description: Intel and AMD CPU drivers, governors, boost, and platform profiles.

settings.description:
Kernel NMI Watchdog
off: saves power, on: for kernel debugging only

groups.title: CPU DRIVER OPMODE
groups.description: Intel/AMD · intel_pstate supports Active or Passive; amd-pstate may also support Guided.

groups.title: CPU SCALING GOVERNOR
groups.description: Intel/AMD · Available governors depend on the active CPU driver. Check tlp-stat -p before changing defaults.

groups.title: CPU SCALING FREQ
groups.description: Intel/AMD · Set frequency limits supported by the active driver. With intel_pstate, prefer performance percentages.

groups.title: CPU ENERGY PERF POLICY
groups.description: Intel only · Select the HWP/EPP or EPB energy policy. Check tlp-stat -p for support.

groups.title: CPU PERF
groups.description: Intel only · Limit CPU performance as a percentage. Requires intel_pstate or intel_cpufreq.

groups.title: CPU BOOST
groups.description: Intel/AMD · Allow or block turbo boost. Enabled permits boost; it does not force it.

groups.title: CPU HWP DYN BOOST
groups.description: Intel only · Dynamic HWP boost requires intel_pstate Active mode and a supported CPU.

groups.title: NMI WATCHDOG
groups.description: Disable to save a small amount of power; enable only for kernel debugging.

groups.title: PLATFORM PROFILE
groups.description: Hardware-dependent · Balance performance, thermals, and fan behavior. Check tlp-stat -p.

groups.title: MEM SLEEP
groups.description: Suspend mode: s2idle wakes faster; deep usually saves more power. Keep the system default if unsure.

categories.name: USB
categories.description: USB autosuspend and device inclusion/exclusion rules.

settings.description: USB autosuspend feature

Exclude listed devices from USB autosuspend (separate with spaces).
Use lsusb to get the ids.
Note: input devices (usbhid) and libsane-supported scanners are excluded automatically

Exclude audio devices from USB autosuspend:
- 0=do not exclude, 1=exclude

Exclude bluetooth devices from USB autosuspend:
- 0=do not exclude, 1=exclude

Exclude phone devices from USB autosuspend:
- 0=do not exclude, 1=exclude (enable charging)

Exclude printers from USB autosuspend:
- 0=do not exclude, 1=exclude

Exclude WWAN devices from USB autosuspend:
- 0=do not exclude, 1=exclude

Allow USB autosuspend for listed devices even if already denylisted or
excluded above (separate with spaces). Use lsusb to get the ids

groups.title: USB AUTOSUSPEND
groups.description: Suspend idle USB devices to reduce power use.

groups.title: USB DENYLIST
groups.description: USB IDs excluded from autosuspend. Find IDs with lsusb and separate them with spaces.

groups.title: USB EXCLUDE AUDIO
groups.description: Keep USB audio devices awake.

groups.title: USB EXCLUDE BTUSB
groups.description: Keep USB Bluetooth adapters awake.

groups.title: USB EXCLUDE PHONE
groups.description: Keep connected phones awake so they can continue charging.

groups.title: USB EXCLUDE PRINTER
groups.description: Keep USB printers awake.

groups.title: USB EXCLUDE WWAN
groups.description: Keep USB WWAN adapters awake.

groups.title: USB ALLOWLIST
groups.description: USB IDs allowed to autosuspend even when another rule excludes them.

settings.description: Restore charge thresholds when AC is unplugged

groups.title: RESTORE THRESHOLDS ON BAT
groups.description: Reapply configured charge thresholds after unplugging AC.
